ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

5. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

6. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

7. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

8. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

10. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

11. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

12. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

13. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

14. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
